text:
maria: Heads-up — BlueHarbor reporting recurring 401s on dedicated for a subset of routes after their token rotation at ~09:00 PT. Customer flagged it as "high" impact. Can we triage hotfix vs next minor?

alex: Seen the notes, thanks. Is this only on their Dedicated account or also on Hosted?

maria: Only Dedicated so far. Support reproduced in our staging mirror using their badge. 401s happen ~30s after rotation and persist until a pod restart.

devon: That sounds like sticky KV cache of auth header somewhere in the runtime. I can repro locally with a simulated rotation.

sarah: If it's a cache invalidation / KV mismatch it's risky to leave for next release — customer is seeing production outages. But hotfix carries rollback risk.

devon: Agreed. Quick notes from my local run: after rotation the connection manager keeps old credentials in in-memory session for new requests to pooled workers. Patch is small: drop session cache on token-change event. I have a draft patch + unit test.

maria: What would be the deploy scope? One dedicated pool -> BlueHarbor only? Or infra change that touches all dedicated accounts?

devon: Implementation is scoped to the dedicated auth wrapper code path. It only changes invalidation logic when rotation event contains "replace_all_sessions": true. We can gate with a feature flag per-customer.

alex: Excellent — feature flag per-customer buys low blast radius. How long to get QA and a canary?

devon: I can open the PR today. QA estimate 3-4h for regression + auth flow tests. Then we can canary to BlueHarbor's pool only.

maria: Proposal: ship hotfix behind ff to BlueHarbor's pool, canary 10% of their traffic for 30m, raise to 100% if no errors. If something goes sideways, immediate kill flag and roll back.

sarah: Sounds good. Need deploy checklist and comms: support + account exec need a one-line status and expected ETA. Also legal/compliance notified due to their contract SLA.

alex: I'll draft the comms. Suggested wording: "We're applying an auth cache invalidation patch to your dedicated pool behind a controlled flag. Expect a brief canary today; we will escalate if anomalies occur."

maria: QA: please include tests that simulate token rotate and validate no request sees stale creds after 5s. Also confirm metrics emitted: auth.failure and auth.rotate.event.

qa-bot: Running pre-checklist: regression suite queued, estimated completion in 3.5h.

devon: Deploy steps (draft):
1) merge PR to release/hotfix branch
2) enable ff for blueharbor-dedicated via console
3) deploy to one podset in the pool
4) monitor auth.failure, 5xx, latency for 30m
5) ramp to 100% or rollback

maria: Monitoring: we need a Grafana panel with baseline overlay + alerts. @deploy-bot can you create a temporary graphite alert for auth.failure > 5/min above baseline for 15m?

deploy-bot: Created alert "blueharbor.auth.failure.delta" -> triggers at +5/min sustained for 15m. Notifying #incidents and oncall.

alex: Comms plan: 1) Notify BlueHarbor AM + support with ETA (T+4h) before canary. 2) Short note to internal stakeholders. 3) After success send root-cause + preventive steps.

sarah: Approvals: product (maria), eng lead (alex), oncall aware. I sign off for hotfix behind ff if QA green.

maria: OK — devon, please open the PR and tag qa + alex. I'll prepare the customer message. If QA hits regressions, we hold and consider scheduled patch in next minor with broader tests.

devon: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pulls/4821 — includes tests and a ff gate. Tagging @qa-team @alex.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll post the customer ETA in 30m. :thumbsup:
